rationale: GOG is unusually transparent about licensing versus ownership, explicitly stating in Section 2.1 that users receive a 'personal license' rather than ownership, with plain-language explanations and side summaries. However, marketing still uses 'buy' while legal terms grant only revocable licenses. Protections include statutory refunds, EU withdrawal rights, downloadable DRM-free backups, and moderation appeals—offsetting moderate unilateral powers like suspension rights and service termination clauses.
evidence_quotes: We give you and other GOG users the personal right (known legally as a 'license') to use GOG services...This license is for your personal use. We can stop or suspend this license in some situations.
You have no property interest or right or title in any Virtual Goods, which remains the appropriate publisher's property.
If we have to stop providing access to GOG services and GOG content permanently...you should be able to download any GOG content you purchased.
During that time you should be able to download and safely store all your DRM-free content.
